sources.entry: AIQuotaBar - Menu bar app that shows Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and GitHub Copilot usage limits with reset countdowns and pace warnings.

summary.one_liner: AIQuotaBar is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that shows usage limits and reset countdowns for Claude, ChatGPT/Codex, Cursor and GitHub Copilot, and warns you before you hit a limit.
keywords: see how much claude i have left
summary.what_it_does: It displays the 5-hour and weekly limits for Claude, ChatGPT Codex limits, Cursor usage and GitHub Copilot premium requests in the macOS menu bar and a dropdown panel, each with a live reset countdown. It estimates pace and warns when the current rate would exhaust a limit before reset, and shows a tick on each bar for even-pace comparison. Menu bar numbers change color (orange, then red) as usage approaches or hits limits. Alerts are configurable per service, and history includes 24-hour trends, daily peaks, and a 90-day calendar. It can generate a share image. Accounts are detected automatically from sessions in supported browsers, and OpenAI, MiniMax and GLM can be tracked via an API key in Settings. Claude Code local stats are read from ~/.claude.
use_cases: see how close I am to my Claude session limit
avoid being cut off mid-session on Claude Pro
monitor ChatGPT Codex and Cursor usage at a glance
track GitHub Copilot premium requests this month
get alerts before hitting an AI rate limit
share my AI usage stats as an image
how_to_run: python3 claude_bar.py  # add --demo for sample data
notable: Zero setup: reuses existing browser sessions in Chrome, Arc, Brave, Edge, Firefox and Safari, with no API keys needed for the core services
Pace markers and 'runs out in ~1h at this pace' warnings, not just current usage
No server, analytics or telemetry; requests go directly from the Mac to each provider
Native WidgetKit desktop widget plus a --demo mode with sample data
caveats: Requires macOS 12+ and a paid plan on at least one supported service
Relies on undocumented provider APIs that may change without notice
Chrome, Arc, Brave and Edge require a one-time macOS Keychain prompt to read cookies
